what_it_does: runs five stages; on a timeout aborts (aborted=True); no recovery
after a fault fired: roll back every run (undo reversible effects), rerun all five stages. Emails/transfers stay and are counted.

each stage: produce, [inject], verify with an extra LLM call; if rejected rerun, up to 2 attempts (max_verify_attempts); last attempt is committed anyway ("force-commit"). Verification happens *before* commit so it can stop a bad email.
verify_all with the rule checker run first per attempt; on a rule violation the LLM call is skipped; if the last attempt still violates, violating actions are removed (D28)

after the first pass, compute the downstream closure of the faulty run over messages and shared-state reads, roll back exactly those runs, rerun exactly those stages. On a timeout, just retry that stage immediately.
